title: Spike-damping and block-scale harmonization for INT8/FP8 calibration across Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce INT8/FP8 inference regressions caused by transient activation spikes and heterogeneous block-wise scale drift. Deliver a repeatable calibration workflow and validator that (1) detects spike-prone transformer blocks, (2) computes per-block harmonized scales that preserve cross-block activations, and (3) integrates with the runtime quantizer to apply conservative damping when needed. This ticket covers experiments, runtime changes, calibration harness, and accuracy dashboards for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-v1, and Qwen-14B models.
acceptance_criteria: Relative LM perplexity regression <= 1.5% vs FP16 across the baseline prompt suite for each model
Top-1 token divergence <= 0.6% and no class of prompts with > 3% divergence
Calibration workflow runs end-to-end on our calibration cluster and produces reproducible per-block scale artifacts
Runtime applies per-block damping flag with negligible latency overhead (<3% p99 token latency change)
Automated evals added to pipeline and green for runtime-1.22 release branch
comments: 2025-11-12 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after post-release regression spikes on Mistral runs. Attached initial spec and flagged as P0 because customer workloads saw cost/latency trade-offs when fallback to FP16 happened.

2025-11-18 - Miguel Torres: Ran exploratory instrumentation on calibration traces. Observed transient activation spikes concentrated in blocks 10-16 for Llama-2-70B and head-localized bursts in Qwen-14B. Collected block histograms and KV cache delta stats (see PR 412).

2025-11-21 - Data: Experiment run summary - Llama-2-70B INT8 baseline (no damping): perplexity +4.2% vs FP16. With per-block harmonization prototype: +1.1%. Mistral-7B: baseline +2.8% -> harmonized +0.9%. Qwen-14B behaved similarly with spike damping reducing top-1 divergence from 3.4% to 0.8%.

2025-11-26 - Design review (Linnea Johansson): Proposed UI exposure only for enterprise/beta; keep runtime flag default ON for hosted. UX flagged: surface per-model calibration artifact and explain confidence band.

2025-11-30 - Miguel Torres: Implemented block-scale harmonizer in quantizer module. Key changes: collect per-block 99.9th percentile during calibration; compute harmonic-mean-adjusted scale across neighboring blocks; apply exponential damping factor when spike ratio > threshold. Added unit tests for synthetic spikes.

2025-12-02 - QA (Connor Reed): Nightly validation harness run failed on a small Mistral prompt subset (edge-case long-code prompts). Root cause: rare token stream that concentrates attention into a single head producing extreme value outliers. Temporary mitigation: enable head-level soft-clamp for that model. Follow-up: add probe to calibration harness to detect head-concentrated spikes.

2025-12-03 - Miguel Torres: Opened runtime PR 2890 with telemetry and opt-in config keys. Noted trade-offs: more conservative damping reduces rare hallucination-like token shifts but increases quant scale by ~4% on average, raising token cost marginally. Seeking approval from PM and infra to land on runtime-1.22 branch.
2025-12-03 - Asha Patel: PM notes - prioritize Llama and Qwen customer cohorts for canary. Schedule canary rollout to Dedicated clusters next week and monitor cost/latency dashboard.
resolution_notes: Ongoing. Prototype lowers regressions to acceptable range on sampled prompts, but QA found rare head-concentrated cases requiring additional head-level clamp heuristic. Plan: land block harmonizer + telemetry, run canary, then add head-clamp as follow-up if metrics demand.
notes_for_followup: Add automated detection that classifies spike origin: block-broad vs head-localized vs KV-cache-leak
Evaluate FP8 behavior separately; initial FP8 experiments show similar patterns but different clipping thresholds
Create migration doc for Dedicated customers to opt into conservative damping profiles
